rationale:
dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=1234, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=800, outer_wall_s=3000, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, rationale=iter-8 CEILING-DOCUMENTATION PROBE (per-scan step count) toward the iter-20 hard stop -- NOT hr-chasing. Change EXACTLY ONE knob: n_iter 400 -> 800 (double the per-scan Adam steps in _fit_one_scene). Everything else returns to the iter-1 canonical 6-param config: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3 (iter-7 confirmed warm-start DEPTH inert at 8 ep -> 0.946953, so revert to 3 for a clean A/B isolating the per-scan-step axis), img_n_bf=proj_n_bf=1, all sigmas at Wagner defaults, lr=5e-3, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=6, seed=1234 (iter-6-confirmed stable).

STATE: CONVERGED to the 6-param structural ceiling. 7 iters all flat at SSIM ~0.9462-0.9470 @1, hr 0 (PSNR ~35.6 dB, ~1 dB BELOW the LD-FBP baseline 36.56 dB): iter-1 0.946237, iter-2 (img_n_bf 1->3) 0.945237, iter-3 (img_sr 0.02->0.005) 0.946177, iter-4 (proj_sr 0.02->0.0005) 0.945745, iter-5 (warm_start OFF) 0.945955, iter-6 (seed 42->1234) 0.946157, iter-7 (pretrain_epochs 3->8) 0.946953 (a tiny +0.0008, still hr 0, still below FBP). This matches the documented dd-bf-supervised structural ceiling (capped 0.9502 with the SAME 6 BF params, every scalar flat).

FAILURE MODE (structural, not a tuning miss): the 6-param bilateral cannot beat an already-clean dense-view (2304-angle) FBP -- the half-view N2I information loss (each per-scan fit only ever sees a 1152-angle subset of the scan) exceeds what 6 trainable bilateral params can denoise, so no sigma/depth/warm_start/seed/warm-start-depth setting clears hr=0. The remaining iters to iter-20 are CEILING DOCUMENTATION (probes that show WHY the ceiling holds), not optimization.

WHY THIS KNOB / NEW AXIS (untried): all 7 prior iters probed BF sigma/depth (iter-2,3,4), warm_start PRESENCE on/off (iter-5), RNG/val-draw (iter-6), and warm-start DEPTH/pretrain_epochs (iter-7). n_iter -- the per-scan Adam STEP COUNT -- has stayed at 400 every iter. It is the ONE remaining untried structural axis: per-scan FIT BUDGET, distinct from both warm-start presence (iter-5) and warm-start depth (iter-7). The campaign-state insight is that raising n_iter HURTS the U-Net N2I via per-scan OVERFIT (_fit_one_scene has no early-stop), but the 6-param bilateral physically CANNOT overfit a single scan (only 6 trainable params), so this probe tests the opposite hypothesis cleanly: with no overfit risk, does a doubled per-scan fit budget let the BF reach a BETTER per-scan optimum, or does it converge to the SAME below-FBP optimum? Either way it bounds the ceiling along the per-scan-step axis.

EXPECTATION (success condition for a ceiling-documentation probe): a doubled per-scan budget (800 steps) is expected to land at essentially the SAME ~0.9462 @1, hr 0 -- the 6-param BF has so few DOF that 400 steps already converges the per-scan fit, so 800 should be flat. A flat result CONFIRMS the ceiling is invariant to per-scan fit budget: the limit is the BF's 6-param CAPACITY vs the 2304-view FBP and the half-view N2I info loss, NOT under-optimization of the per-scan fit. By construction this adds NO trainable capacity and (unlike the U-Net) carries NO overfit risk, so it cannot escape the ceiling -- it can only bound it along the per-scan-step axis. This is ceiling-documentation toward the iter-20 hard stop, not hr-chasing.

Per-image N2I (commit 1f4c3394): short amortized warm-start pre-pass (3 ep x 200 train) then per-scan Adam fit (NOW 800 steps) on each val scan's OWN half-angle measurements (GT-free), scored by evaluate_calibrated on the SAME L277 val scenes as every other Mayo method. NOT amortized train-then-forward. Wall <=15 min target: iter-1 ran 469s at n_iter=400/val_n=6; doubling per-scan steps ~ doubles the per-scan fit time (~300s -> ~600s) + ~75s warm-start ~ 675s ~ 11-12 min, within the 1h sbatch wall and the <=15 min soft target.
